events.author: Veikko Vikkelä
events.text:
Hi Erkki, I'm at the site now. Changed the SFP on transmission node TRN-042.
Link is up and alarms cleared, but traffic is still not coming back. Have you seen this before?

events.author: Erkki Expert
events.text: Yes. Is this one of the older units?

events.author: Veikko Vikkelä
events.text: Yes, installed around 2019 I think.

events.author: Erkki Expert
events.text:
Ok. Don't trust the green link status on those.
Sometimes after changing the SFP the interface comes up normally, but the forwarding state doesn't recover correctly.

events.author: Veikko Vikkelä
events.text: So another SFP?

events.author: Erkki Expert
events.text:
No. Usually the SFP is fine.
Check whether the traffic counters are actually increasing. If they stay at zero even though the interface is UP, it's probably the issue I've seen before.

events.author: Veikko Vikkelä
events.text: Yes. Link UP. RX power looks normal. Counters basically zero.

events.author: Erkki Expert
events.text:
That's it.
Disable the interface, wait a little, then enable it again. Don't reboot the whole unit unless that fails.

events.author: Veikko Vikkelä
events.text: Did that. Traffic is back 👍

events.author: Erkki Expert
events.text: Good. These old units sometimes behave like this after an optical module replacement.

events.author: Veikko Vikkelä
events.text: Is this documented somewhere?

events.author: Erkki Expert
events.text:
Not that I know of 😄
We've just learned it over the years.

events.author: Erkki Expert
events.text:
Subject: RE: TRN-042 traffic not recovering after SFP replacement

Hi Veikko,

That sounds like the behaviour we have seen with some of the older transmission units.

The confusing part is that everything can look normal after replacing the optical module:

- interface status = UP
- optical levels = OK
- alarms = cleared

...but traffic still doesn't recover.

Before replacing the SFP again or rebooting the unit, check the traffic counters.

If the interface is UP but the counters remain at zero, try disabling and enabling the interface once.

This has solved the issue in several cases I've seen.

I don't think this is written in the normal field instructions. It is one of those things we have learned from experience.

Regards,
Erkki

events.text: Moi Jari, I just changed the SFP on TRN-042 at site OULU-07. The link is showing up, alarms cleared and optics levels look totally normal, but there is absolutely no traffic passing through.

events.author: Veikko Vikkelä
events.text: Traffic counters are at zero too. Any ideas what could be wrong here?

events.text: Moi Veikko. Just swap the SFP again, it's always the optic in these cases.

events.author: Jari Korhonen
events.text: Don't bother with bouncing the interface or rebooting the node, a second SFP always fixes it.

events.author: Veikko Vikkelä
events.text: Okay, sounds simple enough. I will grab another SFP from the van and put it in now.

events.text: Moi Erkki, I just swapped the SFP on TRN-063 here at OULU-11. The link is up, alarms cleared and optics look ok, but all counters are zero and no traffic is passing through.

events.author: Veikko Vikkelä
events.text: Moi Erkki, I'm at site OULU-11 working on TRN-087. I just replaced the SFP, and the link is up now with good RX power, but traffic counters are staying at zero.

events.author: Veikko Vikkelä
events.text: By the way TRN-034 had a dispatch last week too, different thing though. But yeah, this TRN-087 is acting weird now.

events.author: Erkki Expert
events.text: Moi Veikko! Let me check the node from here. Yes, I see the link state is up and optical levels look totally normal.

events.author: Erkki Expert
events.text: This is a known quirk with these units. When the link is up and optics are normal after an SFP change but counters stay at zero, you should just disable the interface, wait a bit, and then enable it again. Don't reboot the unit and don't swap the SFP again.

events.author: Veikko Vikkelä
events.text: Ah okay, good to know. I was just about to swap the SFP again to be sure, glad I asked first. Let me try disabling the port now.

events.author: Veikko Vikkelä
events.text: Okay, port is disabled. Waitng for a moment...

events.author: Veikko Vikkelä
events.text: Now enabled it back. Hey, the traffic counters started incrementing immediately! :)

events.author: Erkki Expert
events.text: Excellent, traffic is flowing normally now. That bounce always clears the stuck buffer on TRN-087 after a hot-swap. Good job!

events.text: Moi Erkki! I just replaced the SFP on TRN-019 here at OULU-03. The link is physically up, alarms cleared and optics look normal, but all traffic counters are staying at zero.

events.author: Erkki Expert
events.text: Moi Timo. Ah, that is one of those old TX-200 units from 2016. They have this weird bug sometimes with new SFPs.

events.author: Erkki Expert
events.text: Try to disable the interface, wait about 30 seconds, and then enable it again. Don't reboot the node, the port bounce usually does the trick.

events.author: Timo Laine

events.author: Timo Laine
events.text: Tried the bounce, didn't help. Counters still stuck at zero after the disable/enable.

events.author: Timo Laine
events.text: Had to reboot in the end. After the reboot TRN-019 is working fine and traffic is flowing normally now.

events.author: Erkki Expert
events.text: Hm, so the bounce didn't work on that one, odd. Usually it is enough, but good that the reboot fixed it anyway!
